rationale: Ezekiel 22:30 (BSB) reads: 'I searched for a man among them to repair the wall and stand in the gap before Me on behalf of the land, so that I should not destroy it. But I found no one.' Keil and Delitzsch, on that verse, hold that 'the intercession of Abraham for Sodom' was 'floating before the mind of Ezekiel, since the concluding words of the verse contain an obvious allusion to Genesis 18:28.' They credit the observation to Hitzig while recording that Hitzig denied the verse means intercession at all. Their printed reference for the intercession reads 'Genesis 18:13.'; on Ezekiel 14:14 the same commentary prints '(Genesis 18:23.)', so 18:23ff. is probably meant. The other commentaries on the same page point elsewhere. Ellicott, Jamieson-Fausset-Brown, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary cite Psalm 106:23, where Moses 'stood before Him in the breach to divert His wrath from destroying them' (BSB), and Barnes likewise names Moses. Gill mentions Abraham only in passing, in a list: 'as Abraham for Sodom, Moses for Israel.' The Cambridge Bible reads Ezekiel's figure differently: 'A “man” here is not a man to intercede, but a man to interpose.' Bible Hub's interlinear shows that the terms shared with Genesis 18 ('destroy,' shachat; 'stand ... before,' ʿamad lifne) also appear in Psalm 106:23, which in addition has Ezekiel's word 'breach' (perets); only 'find' (matsa) is shared with Genesis 18 and not with the psalm. Graded allusion because Ezekiel names no one, and plausible because only one commentary read argues for Genesis 18 specifically while most point to the Moses psalm. The same grading reasoning is used in conn-gen11-babel-zephaniah3: a link drawn by some named commentators but not by others on the same verse.
